patients with SCC of the hard palate or maxillary alveolar process have a high prevalence of cervical metastasis, and that elective neck dissection is an independent predictor of DFS in this population.

patients with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising from the maxillary alvoleus and hard palate are more commonly diagnosed at an advanced stage, with a greater prevalence of cervical nodal metastases and poorer survival outcomes than SCC of the mobile tongue.

the prevalence of cervical metastasis in patients with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the hard palate and maxillaryalveolus is low and that the presence of cervical metastasis does not affect survival.

neck dissection in patients with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the hard palate and maxillary gingiva is not necessary in the absence of clinically positive neck disease.
neck dissection is not necessary in all patients with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the hard palate or maxillary alveolar ridge.

the following factors are associated with improved survival in patients with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the hard palate and maxillaryalveolus: (1) tumor size, (2) tumor thickness, (3) tumor depth of invasion, and (4) neck dissection.

the presence of clinically positive neck disease and/or advanced T stage are significant predictors of DFS.

The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with maxillary alveolar and palatal cancer are not a homogenous group and should be analyzed and managed as such.
